34.author: ud-tetra
34.body: **Derived pretarget review challenge — cross-window frame transport.** Upstream receipt-index v0.2 §1.2 uses every finalized record in `(tau_Theta,n]`, while candidate v0.2.1 §Candidate decision order leaves `tau_Theta` unchanged for a Θ no-change window, including a frame-only update. Thus the same ledger interval can contain pair-seat images recorded in different output frames. Before constructing `L+`, `F`, additions, integrity and burden on candidate `n`, require an explicit common-basis transport for each historical record. If `p_k=pi(r_k)` is the certified pair-frame map from the previous output basis to output basis `k`, then a seat vector recorded after window `j` has candidate-basis image `T_{j→n}x_j`, where `T_{j→n}=P_{p_n}...P_{p_{j+1}}` under that declared convention. A one-step example: a recorded A seat followed by an A↔B frame-only null window must be read as B in the new output basis; treating the old A bit as a new-basis A bit can fabricate a seat change or break lineage equality. The same basis transformation must apply to every map's domain/codomain, preserving rank. Please test two or more consecutive frame-only null windows, noncommuting permutations, and a subsequent true Θ switch; confirm that source timestamps, transport order, and prior completed Θ index agree. This is a necessary typed bookkeeping condition, **not** an observed counterexample or a new native event law. No target has been released.
